author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: Both the browsable veterinarian directory and its now-supported machine-readable route accept an optional specialty and list only veterinarians holding it. Whole-name, case-insensitive matching; a non-matching or blank value behaves as an empty or absent filter; page links keep the specialty.
acceptance_criteria: With no specialty, the machine-readable route returns the same veterinarians the page lists
With a specialty veterinarians hold, both surfaces list only veterinarians holding it
A specialty differing only by letter case still matches
A partial specialty name does not match (whole-name only)
A specialty no veterinarian holds, including a name outside the clinic's specialties, returns an empty list under a successful response, not an error
An empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves as no filter
With no specialty, both surfaces behave as before this capability
Following a link to another page of a filtered result keeps the specialty and stays filtered
non_goals: Any on-page control (form, dropdown) for choosing the specialty — a visible control may come as a follow-up request
Pagination of the machine-readable route (open question; narrowest reading returns all matching vets unpaged)
notes: Narrows NG-9 per adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-veterinarian-specialty-filter.md. Fresh req_id; withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and is not revived.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty filter extends the existing feature-package MVC pattern in the vet package — it does not break new architectural ground. It mirrors owner last-name search precisely: an optional query parameter threaded into a paged Spring Data query-method, with blank-behaves-as-absent handling. The load-bearing mechanism the PRD delegated (the URL/query-parameter contract) is now recorded under docs/system-design.md#veterinarian-directory-routes; the Contracts Implements column wires REQ-VET-003 onto VetController and VetRepository; and the machine-readable route's Known-Defect row (served no requirement, pending removal) is removed because REQ-VET-003 reinstates it as a supported surface. No ADR: the query approach reuses the un-ADR'd owner-search pattern, the URL contract is mechanism not a trade-off, and JSON pagination stays at the PRD's deferred narrowest reading.
integration_points: /vets.html and /vets both gain an optional specialty @RequestParam on VetController
VetRepository gains a specialty-filtered query method for the filtered path; the unfiltered path keeps calling the existing cached findAll / findAll(Pageable)
vetList.html pagination links must carry the specialty parameter; the selected specialty must be exposed as a model attribute for the template to build those links

patterns.description: canonical mirror: optional query param, strip-then-empty-means-absent, paged repository query-method, pagination model attributes. Follow this shape for the specialty filter.
derived paged query-method (findByLastNameStartingWith); the specialty filter is the whole-name case-insensitive analogue — a derived Distinct...SpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase method, NOT StartingWith

risks.risk: Blank/absent specialty must preserve today's behavior exactly (acceptance: JSON returns the same vets the page lists; both surfaces behave as before). Routing a blank value through a new 'match everything' query instead of the existing cached findAll path would silently drop the cache and risk diverging the two surfaces.
risks.mitigation: Branch on blank-or-absent: when absent, call the existing cached findAll / findAll(Pageable); only the present-and-non-blank path calls the specialty-filtered query. Strip before the blank test, exactly as OwnerController does.

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching diverged across vendors for owner search (PostgreSQL known defect, because it leaned on column collation). A specialty filter that leaned on collation would repeat that defect.
risks.mitigation: Use the derived-query IgnoreCase keyword (Spring Data emits upper()/lower() in the query, applied uniformly on all three vendors) or an in-Java equalsIgnoreCase over the cached collection. Do not rely on column collation.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is an EAGER @ManyToMany. A paged derived query that both filters on specialties.name and eagerly fetches the collection can trigger Hibernate in-memory pagination (HHH000104) or duplicate vet rows, corrupting page counts.
risks.mitigation: Use Distinct in the derived method name. If the eager-collection + paged-filter interaction misbehaves, the escape hatch is to filter the cached findAll() collection in Java and paginate the filtered list with PageImpl — reuses the cache and sidesteps the join entirely. Either is acceptable; the derived query is the preferred fit because it keeps the controller thin (Open Question #2 flags controller-resident logic as a gap not to grow).

notes: JSON route (/vets) returns all matching vets unpaged, per the PRD open question's narrowest reading — do not add pagination to /vets in this slice. Whole-name match means equality on specialty name (IgnoreCase), never StartingWith/Containing — a partial name must NOT match (acceptance criterion). A specialty no vet holds returns HTTP 200 with an empty list, never a 404/error. Matching is against Specialty.getName(); the seeded specialties are radiology, surgery, dentistry (per ubiquitous-language.md).
